HEADLINE: all four fitters are statistically indistinguishable on held-out error: overall median absolute error 377.08-377.44 and RMSE 858.29-859.17 across 1197 rows whose p90 absolute error is ~1170. The spread between fitters is ~0.4 medAE against an error scale of ~377. Fitter choice does not move overall accuracy.
THE_ONE_REAL_SIGNAL: at picks 46-64 (n=345) the LOCAL-LINEAR boundary treatment beats the kernel: control 265.85 and loclin 265.35 median absolute error against 291.15 for the shipped kernel (distfirst) and 282.19 for powerspine — about 9% better. This is out-of-sample confirmation of the boundary argument: the shipped kernel window is one-sided at the pick-64 edge, borrows from higher-valued interior picks, and biases the tail UP. At picks 1-10 the ordering reverses and the kernel is best (877.87 vs 886.45 loclin, 911.70 powerspine). control is the kernel at the head and local-linear at the tail, i.e. best in both zones.
disclosed_comparability_asymmetry: no fitter pinned inside fold_fit (all pick-1 held-out predictions sit in 2900-3100, not at 3000), so the scores are comparable. One asymmetry stands: powerspine MONOTONISES its fold predictions (PAVA + descent) while the other three do not — median-by-pick non-monotone steps are 5 for powerspine against 10-11 for the others. That is part of what its method IS, it is disclosed, and it should be read as a property of the arm rather than an unfair advantage.

control.boundary_rule: off-domain nominal kernel mass > 1.0% (log-pick distance to edge < 2.3263*h)

loclin.cond_matrix: normalised X'WX (weights / S0, distances / h) — dimensionless
loclin.fallback_rule: cond(normalised) > cond_threshold, or a non-finite ridged solve -> local weighted mean sum(Wv)/sum(W) at that pick
loclin.ridge_applied_to: slope entry A[1,1] only, as RIDGE_REL * S0 * h^2 (never the intercept)

powerspine.residual_bandwidth_policy: H.bandwidth_at: hmin=0.10 -> hmax=0.60 in 0.02 steps until effective n >= 35

distfirst_is_the_kernel_by_identity.counterfactual: with a 1.5x conditional-mean bandwidth the arm deviates by up to 260.45, so the machinery is live; the common-bandwidth policy makes it degenerate.
distfirst_is_the_kernel_by_identity.its_real_contribution: the decomposition, which is new evidence in its own right
distfirst_is_the_kernel_by_identity.verified_by_integrator: max |rate x condmean - kernel_mean| over picks 1..64 = 2.27e-13
distfirst_is_the_kernel_by_identity.why: rate = sum(W.1{v>0})/sum(W) and condmean = sum(W.v)/sum(W.1{v>0}), so the indicator cancels and the product IS the kernel mean whenever both components share a bandwidth. The panel therefore carries THREE distinct price readings, not four.

establishment_decomposition.note: from the distfirst arm; new evidence
establishment_decomposition.reading: the late picks are cheap mainly because 44% never establish; those who do are worth ~495. Same shape as the pool levels, where the median is zero and the mean is carried by a minority.

fitter_descriptions.control: shipped Gaussian log-pick kernel (H.kernel_raw, alpha=1, plain weighted mean) with a degree-1 local-linear WLS boundary correction over log(pick) applied only where >1.0% of the kernel's nominal weight falls off the pick domain [1,64] (log-distance to edge < 2.3263*h): boundary width = picks 1-2 at the low edge and picks 51-64 at the high edge on this matrix; interior picks 3-50 are the shipped kernel exactly; bandwidth from H.bandwidth_at() (harness policy).
fitter_descriptions.distfirst: distribution-first: raw(pick) = rate(pick) * E[value|established,pick], both Gaussian kernels over log(pick) at alpha=1; establishment indicator is the harness definition (value>0); bandwidth policy H.bandwidth_at(nmin=35, hmin=0.10, hmax=0.60) applied per component to its own population — rate over ALL rows, conditional mean over ESTABLISHED rows only (disclosed: on this population both searches select the SAME h at all 64 picks, so the recombination equals the plain kernel mean to float precision — max abs deviation 4.5e-13); isotonic weights = unconditional kernel effective n
fitter_descriptions.loclin: local-linear (degree-1 WLS) on log(pick) with Gaussian weights at every pick 1..64, bandwidth from harness_pvc.bandwidth_at (nmin=35, h in [0.10,0.60] step 0.02); slope-only ridge RIDGE_REL=1e-06*S0*h^2, fallback to local weighted mean when cond(normalised X'WX) > COND_MAX=1000000.0; isotonic weights = local effective n; alpha=1, plain WLS, no CE aggregator
fitter_descriptions.powerspine: power-law spine A*pick^-B (WLS of log(per-pick mean) on log(pick), the 265 zero-value rows kept at full weight inside those means so the log of a zero is never taken) fitted on the SUB-RANGE picks 8-64 with BREAK POINT = 8 (first pick where the shipped bandwidth policy sits on its floor) and held FLAT at spine(8) below the break rather than extrapolated, plus additive residuals smoothed with the shipped bandwidth policy — RESIDUAL BANDWIDTH h(p) in log(pick) units, grown from hmin=0.10 in 0.02 steps until nmin=35 effective rows, capped hmax=0.60, realised as h=0.60/0.36/0.26/0.20/0.16/0.14/0.12 at picks 1-7 and h=0.10 at every pick 8-64 — then recombined, clipped at 0 and forced monotone non-increasing (PAVA on effective-n weights, then a 1.0-unit strict descent over plateaus) before the harness's pin; alpha=1, no CE aggregator

harness.establishment_definition: the matrix own classification: no season with games >= 6
harness.screening: every fitter re-run by the integrator in the pinned env; all four byte-identical to the subagent output. Harness integrity re-verified functionally before each judging step (the shipped-kernel reference still reproduces the ruled ladder 4fc40e91).

positive_signed_error_is_arithmetic.reading: every fitter shows a positive median signed error (+153 to +340 by range). That is what a MEAN fit must do on a right-skewed population where 22% of rows are exactly zero and 67% sit below the mean. It is arithmetic, near-identical across all four, and is NOT evidence of fitter bias.

smoothness.note: powerspine is far the smoothest and that is a real, non-accuracy advantage
smoothness.reading: powerspine hands over an already strictly-descending curve (0 raw violations, 1 forced pick, and that one only because its raw pick 2 of 3045.4 exceeds the 3000 pin). The other three need 6-7 violations pooled and 8-9 picks nudged. Every arm is non-monotone at picks 1-3, independently: picks 1-3 are genuinely unresolved in the data (effective n 34-38).

status: REPORT-ONLY panel evidence. No fitter is adopted; alpha=1 throughout this experiment.
